memory_update.text: SPSC should be tracked as an underfollowed retail supply-chain network candidate: high recurring customer base, trading-partner network effects, and embedded retailer/supplier integrations map closely to omnichannel order orchestration.
MANH remains the clearest reference public company for OMS/WMS/omnichannel execution, but valuation and attention may be higher than the desired underfollowed lane.
DSGX is an adjacent logistics/compliance execution candidate; include in later layers only if evidence shows ecommerce shipping, fulfillment, or retail delivery-promise exposure is material.
ZBRA represents the physical data-capture layer beneath OMS/WMS: inventory visibility, RFID, scanners, and mobile workflows may be a second-order bottleneck for omnichannel promise accuracy.
Need deeper verification of pure-play smaller OMS/WMS vendors because many are private, Canadian-listed, OTC, or embedded inside larger enterprise software suites; avoid overfitting to ticker memory.

node: Omnichannel order orchestration and supply-chain execution software
summary: Expanded the omnichannel order orchestration node toward scarce software, network, logistics-data, and edge-infrastructure providers. The strongest underfollowed lane candidates are not consumer-facing retailers but embedded execution-layer vendors: supply-chain execution SaaS, retail EDI/trading networks, logistics visibility/compliance networks, and inventory-capture hardware/software that makes store and warehouse fulfillment data usable. No buy/sell view is implied.
